thought: a masked little creature near the fur stall; Baraek prices anything with fur
line: Keep that creature clear of the fur stall. Baraek might price it.

thought: the creature is sniffing about; the tea seller shouts at anyone touching his cups
line: Hello, little one. Don't you go near the tea stall cups.

thought: pointing it out to a friend in the street
line: Here, look at that, a little bandit trotting along behind.

thought: speaker clutches their basket as it passes
line: Hand on the shopping, I think, till that's gone past.

thought: it keeps looking at the stalls like it knows how they work
line: Must be a city creature, that, the way it's eyeing the stalls.

thought: the square already has its thieves; now a four-legged one
line: As if the square hadn't enough thieves working it already.

thought: heard these creatures only take up with thieves; says so with a sly look
line: They say those only take to a thief. I'd not like to say more.

thought: wonders whether it obeys or just follows the food
line: Does it come when it's called, or only when there's food out?

thought: first takes it for a cat, then corrects himself
line: Is that a cat? No... a cat wouldn't look that pleased with itself.

thought: thinks of their own cat at home on the sill
line: My cat would have plenty to say about that, from the windowsill.

thought: its coat is glossier than most coats in the square
line: It's got a better coat on than half the square.

thought: guards their own basket of shopping
line: Whatever it's after, it's not getting it out of my basket.

thought: watches its little clever paws working at nothing
line: Those little hands on it. Busy little hands, I'll bet.

thought: the gate guards search suspicious sorts; this one looks suspicious
line: The guards on the gate would search that one, never mind you.

thought: it trots ahead as if it knows the streets
line: Off home, is it? It looks like it knows the way better than you.

thought: sees a beaver in the street and likes its coat
line: Ooh, a beaver! Lovely glossy coat on it, too.

thought: beavers follow those who fell a great many trees; that's hard graft
line: You must've felled half the woods for that one to take to you.

thought: likes beavers for being busy, like a good townsman
line: I do like a beaver. Honest sort of animal, always busy.

thought: talks to the beaver; the church is draughty enough without chewed pews
line: Hello, handsome. Leave the church pews be, it's draughty enough.

thought: points out to a friend how well kept it is
line: Here, that's a beaver. Well kept, too, look at its coat.

thought: thinks of their own firewood
line: Could do with one of those for the firewood, I could.

thought: a beaver must take patience to keep; credits the owner sideways
line: Takes a patient sort to keep a beaver, I should think.

thought: notices its tidy paws
line: Neat little paws on it. Tidy worker, I expect.

thought: wishes for its energy
line: Wish I had half its get-up-and-go, I do.

thought: compares it favourably with the Blue Moon's regulars
line: Better company than most in the Blue Moon, I'd say.

thought: it walks to heel better than the speaker's dog
line: Well, look at that! Walks better to heel than my dog.

thought: a beaver in the city is a rare sight
line: A beaver in the square... you don't see that every day.

thought: its fur beats anything Thessalia has on her rails
line: Smarter coat than anything in Thessalia's shop, that.

thought: a hard worker would have the woodpile stacked
line: It'll have your woodpile stacked by sundown, I shouldn't wonder.

thought: the coat shines; somebody feeds it properly
line: Somebody's feeding that beaver properly. Shines like a chestnut.

thought: a fishing bird in a city with no fish in reach
line: A heron in the city? Nearest fish is on somebody's plate.

thought: a heron follows because of the fishy smell, surely
line: Got a heron following you about. Do you smell that much of fish?

thought: tells a friend the bird stands straighter than its owner
line: Here, that bird's got better posture than its owner.

thought: the heron looks down its beak; blames the owner
line: It looks down its beak at me. Learnt that from you, I expect.

thought: pities the bird for its owner's cooking
line: Poor thing. Does it get fed, or does it watch you eat the catch?

thought: long legs, no talk; the owner's the same
line: All legs and no conversation. The bird's much the same.

thought: a heron is meant to be patient; it gets practice
line: Herons are patient birds. It must get plenty of practice with you.

thought: one more creature in the city: the sewers have rats, now this
line: Rats in the sewers, and now herons in the square.

thought: the bird keeps eyeing the player's empty hands
line: It keeps looking at your hands. Expecting a fish, poor thing.

thought: herons wait all day for one fish; a fitting job for this sort
line: Herons wait all day for one fish. Sounds like your sort of work.

thought: the bird walks in front as if it's in charge
line: Look, the bird's leading. That one's just following.

thought: it stands on one leg to look taller
line: It stands on one leg to look taller than you. It's working.

thought: why a heron, when everyone else has a cat
line: Why a heron? What's wrong with a cat, like everyone else?

thought: misattribution: a fishing bird suggests the owner never fishes
line: A heron's a fishing bird. Have you ever thought of fishing?

thought: heard herons follow keen fishers; grants the keenness only
line: They say herons follow keen fishers. Keen, I'll grant you.

thought: a rock walking behind someone; mentions it, just in case
line: There's a rock walking behind you. I thought I'd mention it.

thought: hears it on the cobbles
line: Mind it on the cobbles. Sounds like a cart going over.

thought: points it out to a friend, who doesn't believe it
line: Here, that stone's following that one. No, look, it's walking.

thought: muses that rocks don't usually do the walking
line: Walked past rocks all my life. Never had one walk past me.

thought: worries about the paving
line: Must weigh a fair bit. The paving'll want looking at.

thought: heard these only break loose for a keen miner
line: They say those only break loose for somebody who's mined a great deal.

thought: bids the little rock good day
line: Good afternoon, little rock. Don't you trip anybody up.

thought: it doesn't talk; that must be restful
line: Not much of a talker, is it? Restful, I should think.

thought: the Grand Exchange would try to sell anything, even this
line: Don't let the Grand Exchange see it. They'd weigh it and sell it.

thought: grumbles at the way of the world
line: Walking rocks now. Whatever next, walking chairs?

thought: trying to find a use for it
line: A rock that follows you about... handy for a doorstop, I suppose.

thought: it was quiet for a rock
line: Didn't hear it coming, for a rock. Quiet on its feet.

thought: the dark wizards hang about the stone circle; they'd want this stone back
line: Keep it away from the dark wizards. They'd stand it in their circle.

thought: takes it for a dog, then sees
line: Is that a dog? No... it's a rock. A rock with legs.

thought: the dogs bark at carts; the rock doesn't
line: Better behaved than the dogs round here, I'll give it that.

thought: Emma at the salon would have nothing to cut
line: You'd be Emma's quickest customer at the salon, I'll bet.

thought: the head shines; it'll rain soon
line: Shines like a new kettle, that head. Put a hat on before it rains.

thought: the Varrock wind has had the hair
line: Lost a fight with the wind, did you? The wind won.

thought: pigeons would like a landing place
line: The pigeons will think that's a lovely place to land.

thought: nudges a friend: the head's been polished for market
line: Here, look at that head. Polished it for market day, I'd say.

thought: no hat, no hair, out in all weathers
line: Bald as an egg and twice as brave, going out without a hat.

thought: Aris reads futures; that head would do for a crystal ball
line: Aris could read your future off that head.

thought: everything sells at the Grand Exchange; perhaps the hair did
line: Was the hair worth more at the Grand Exchange than on you?

thought: asks a question that answers itself
line: Cold up there, is it? Looks it.

thought: squints at the glare
line: Sun's out, so I'll squint, if it's all the same to you.

thought: blames the goblins, who take anything
line: Did a goblin take your hair? They'll take anything, goblins.

thought: the hair has gone away like birds
line: Hair's gone south for the winter, has it?

thought: thinks of a frosty morning
line: Wouldn't want that head on a frosty morning.

thought: rain would run straight off
line: Rain'll run right off that. Saves on a towel, I suppose.

thought: mistakes the head for a helmet, then corrects
line: Is that a helmet? No. No, that's all head.

thought: Thessalia sells clothes and changes outfits for nothing
line: Thessalia sells clothes, you know. She'll even dress you for free.

thought: the pillory is behind the general store; that's likely where this ends
line: Pillory's behind the general store, if that's where you're headed.

thought: muggers work the streets; maybe they took the lot
line: Mugged, were you? They've taken the lot, by the look of it.

thought: tells a friend not to look, then again
line: Here, don't look. No, I said don't look.

thought: keeps eyes front and walks on
line: Eyes front. Eyes front, and walk on.

thought: the pickpockets will find nothing to go at
line: Not much for the pickpockets to go at, I suppose.

thought: the Queen's garden is just over the palace wall
line: The Queen's garden is just over that wall, you know.

thought: lost a bet at the city's favourite pub
line: Lost a bet at the Blue Moon, was it?

thought: someone should give them a sack
line: Has nobody got a spare sack? Somebody give that one a sack.

thought: the Herald loves scandal
line: The Herald will have a field day with that.

thought: calls for help, then corrects what help
line: Somebody fetch a guard. Or a blanket. A blanket, I think.

thought: even the city's tramp keeps something on
line: Even Charlie the Tramp keeps his shirt on.

thought: cold cobbles underfoot
line: Mind the cobbles. They're cold underfoot this time of year.

thought: perhaps they came up out of the sewers
line: Did you come up out of the sewers like that?

thought: getting some air; plenty of it
line: Getting a bit of air, are we? Plenty of it, today.

thought: mistakes the player for the city's tramp, then apologises
line: Is that Charlie the Tramp? No, sorry, my mistake.

thought: doubts they can afford a cup of tea
line: Could you stretch to a cup of tea, or shall I not ask?

thought: the Herald costs fifty coins; offers to tell them what's in it
line: The Herald's fifty coins. I'll tell you what's in it, if you like.

thought: everything sells at the Grand Exchange, but not this
line: That lot'd fetch less at the Grand Exchange than the sack it came in.

thought: Horvik sells real armour; he'd not take this
line: Horvik wouldn't take that in part exchange, I'll tell you that.

thought: warns about muggers, then thinks better of it
line: Mind the muggers. No, on second thoughts, they'll leave you be.

thought: Thessalia changes outfits for free; they'd be first in line
line: Thessalia changes outfits for nothing. You'd be first in line.

thought: the dark wizards set on travellers; maybe they robbed this one
line: Did the dark wizards get you, or did you leave home like that?

thought: fresh adventurers come from Lumbridge, and look it
line: Fresh from Lumbridge, are we? It shows.

thought: tells a friend not to give a coin; it'll go on tea
line: Here, don't give that one a coin. It'll go on tea, mark my words.

thought: can't tell sack from shirt
line: Is it a sack or a shirt? Don't tell me, I'll guess wrong.

thought: patches on patches
line: Patches on the patches. Thrifty, I'll give you that.

thought: Baraek only haggles so far; he won
line: Haggling with Baraek, were you? He won, by the look of it.

thought: the beggar's question, turned round
line: Spare some change? No, I can see you can't.

thought: pities them, but they chose those shoes
line: Poor soul. Still, they chose the shoes, didn't they?

thought: nothing in Horvik's shop comes close
line: Horvik's never had anything that fine in his shop.

thought: would pass for someone from the palace
line: Very smart. You'd pass for one of the palace lot.

thought: the guards might salute by mistake
line: Ooh, very grand. The guards'll be saluting you by mistake.

thought: they've done well; says so plainly
line: Done well for yourself, haven't you? Good for you.

thought: the Grand Exchange sees everything and rarely this much
line: Not often you see that much on one back, even at the Grand Exchange.

thought: nudges a friend about the money on show
line: Here, look at that. That's money, that is.

thought: wonders what it would fetch against their house
line: Wonder what all that would fetch. More than my house, I'd say.

thought: a thief loiters by the south gate; warns warmly
line: Lovely gear. Keep it away from the south gate, mind.

thought: they'd not look out of place next to the king
line: You'd not look out of place next to King Roald, I'll say that.

thought: adventuring clearly pays; wrong trade
line: That's what adventuring pays, is it? I'm in the wrong trade.

thought: not the gear of a new Lumbridge adventurer
line: Proper armour, that. Not the Lumbridge sort.

thought: the Herald should feature them
line: The Herald ought to put you on the front.

thought: measures it in pints at the Blue Moon
line: That'd keep the Blue Moon in ale for a year, that would.

thought: would be scared to sit down in it
line: Cor! I'd be scared to sit down in that lot.

thought: looks like someone the Champions' Guild would let in
line: Champions' Guild sort, are you? You've the look.

thought: the dark wizards at the stone circle set on travellers
line: Dark wizards at the stone circle again, was it?

thought: the nasty chicken at the Champions' Guild
line: Not that nasty chicken at the Champions' Guild, was it?

thought: the sewers are full of rats
line: Up from the sewers? The rats down there don't mess about.

thought: adventurers come back from the Wilderness like this
line: Back from the Wilderness, I expect. They all come back like that.

thought: asks a friend to lend a hand
line: Here, somebody give that one an arm before they go over.

thought: the church is draughty but quiet
line: Church is draughty, but it's quiet, if you need a lie down.

thought: surprised they're walking about
line: Blimey. Should you be up and about like that?

thought: asks, then thinks better of it
line: Have you seen yourself? No, best not, I suppose.

thought: tea with sugar, from the stall by the east bank
line: Tea stall's by the east bank. Sugar in it, for the shock.

thought: the muggers pick on the weak
line: You'll want to sit before the muggers see you like that.

thought: the guards won't carry anyone; the speaker has asked
line: The guards won't carry you, you know. I've asked.

thought: offers the wall
line: Lean on the wall a minute. It's held up worse than you.

thought: asks who did it, then doesn't want to know
line: Who did that to you? No, don't tell me, I'll not sleep.

thought: can't look; looks at the stall instead
line: Oh, I can't look. I'll look at the stall.

thought: someone's been fighting and lost
line: Somebody's been fighting, and it wasn't the other fellow who lost.

thought: the apothecary mixes energy potions
line: The apothecary does energy potions, if you bring him the makings.

thought: nobody runs in Varrock unless chased
line: Running in Varrock? Nobody runs here unless the guards are after them.

thought: asks who's chasing; nobody
line: Who's chasing you? Nobody? Then slow down.

thought: puffing like the bear in the palace grounds
line: Here, that one's puffing like the palace bear.

thought: everyone rushing about
line: Everyone rushing about. Where's the fire, I'd like to know.

thought: tea would sort it
line: Get a cup of tea down you and stand still a minute.

thought: the Grand Exchange will still be there
line: The Grand Exchange'll still be there when you get there, you know.

thought: whatever the sale is, it isn't worth it
line: Whatever's on sale, it's not worth all that.

thought: up and down the square all day; sympathy
line: Up and down the square all day, I expect. I know the feeling.

thought: old-fashioned warning
line: Steady on. You'll do yourself a mischief.

thought: Romeo stops strangers and talks; perhaps they're running from him
line: Running from Romeo? He does go on.

thought: don't stop in the road
line: Don't stop in the road. Lean on something, there's a good sort.

thought: puffed out so early
line: Puffed out, and it's not even noon.

thought: the Wilderness is north of the city; a run there
line: Wilderness run, was it? Can't think why anyone would.

thought: their own knees went like that
line: Knees went like that on me once. Never quite came back.

thought: the Champions' Guild only lets in adventurers with a name
line: The Champions' Guild's that way. Not that they'd let you in.

thought: dark wizards set on weaker travellers
line: Mind the dark wizards going home. They pick on the small ones.

thought: new adventurers come from Lumbridge
line: Just in from Lumbridge, are we? Mind the big city.

thought: the palace bear is caged, presumably for this one's sake
line: The palace bear's kept in a cage for your sake, I expect.

thought: the guard loses men fast, but not that fast
line: The guards are short of men, they say. Not that short.

thought: tells a friend that one's off adventuring, alarmingly
line: Here, that one's off adventuring. Somebody stop it.

thought: adventurers are getting younger and smaller
line: They get younger every year, adventurers. And smaller.

thought: pick a small fight
line: Off to fight something? Pick something small.

thought: the giant rat king in the sewers
line: The rat king in the sewers would use you for a toothpick.

thought: the goblins have been asking
line: Watch out for the goblins. They've been asking after you.

thought: wouldn't trust them with the shopping
line: I'd not trust you to carry my shopping home.

thought: Wally beat a demon; this one would struggle with less
line: Wally saw off a demon. You'd struggle with the paperwork.

thought: not a fighting face
line: Not a fighting face, is it? That's a fetching-and-carrying face.

thought: who chases whom with the chickens
line: Do the chickens chase you, or is it the other way about?

thought: the Wilderness is just north; not for this one
line: You'd want a few more dinners in you before the Wilderness.

thought: the tea seller charges ten coins
line: Tea's gone up again at the stall. Ten coins for a cup, ten!

thought: the Herald costs fifty and is mostly the palace
line: Fifty coins for the Herald, and half of it's about the palace.

thought: some grumble about the king; won't commit
line: Some say the king's not much good. I couldn't possibly comment.

thought: the church is cold and the regulars sleep
line: Church was freezing again. Even the regulars slept through it.

thought: Baraek won't haggle past a point
line: Baraek wouldn't come down on the furs. Family to feed, he says.

thought: the caged bear in the palace grounds
line: That bear's been at it all morning at the palace. Somebody feed it.

thought: off to the Grand Exchange later
line: Off to the Grand Exchange later. It's like a fair in there, always.

thought: has never been to Falador; smaller, they say
line: Never been to Falador. Smaller than here, they say.

thought: lost a glove on the way
line: Lost a glove somewhere between the square and the east bank.

thought: their feet
line: My feet. Up and down this square since breakfast.

thought: Aris read their fortune for a coin
line: Aris says I'll come into money. She said that last year as well.

thought: the manhole east of the palace and what lives below
line: Mind the manhole by the palace. There's all sorts down there.

thought: Elsie knits and wants a cup of tea for a story
line: Took old Elsie her cup of tea. Got the Wise Old Man story again.

thought: the Blue Moon was busy last night
line: Blue Moon was heaving last night. My head's still in there.

thought: the Cooks' Guild pie shop is only for proper cooks
line: Cooks' Guild won't let me near the pies. Not a proper cook, they say.

thought: Romeo stops strangers to talk about Juliet; speaker only wanted bread
line: Romeo's been at me again about Juliet. I only came out for bread.

thought: Juliet's father won't hear of Romeo
line: Juliet's father won't hear of Romeo. Can't say I blame him.

thought: Romeo stops anyone who'll stand still
line: Romeo stops anyone who'll stand still. Keep walking, is my advice.

thought: she's on a balcony, he's in the square
line: She's up on a balcony, he's down in the square. Neither of them moves.

thought: sick of the name
line: If I hear the name Juliet once more today...

thought: warns a friend not to catch Romeo's eye
line: Here, don't catch Romeo's eye. He'll start.

thought: Romeo is dense but harmless
line: Poor Romeo. Brains of a turnip, heart of gold.

thought: the Leptoc mansion is by the west bank, if anyone asks
line: The Leptoc place is just past the west bank, if anyone's asking.

thought: love is lovely from a distance
line: Love's a lovely thing. From a distance. A good long distance.

thought: Romeo asked about a Juliet the speaker has never met
line: Romeo asked had I seen Juliet. I've never seen Juliet in my life.

thought: the Herald loves scandal; this would sell
line: The Herald should do a piece on Romeo. It'd sell, I'll say that.

thought: someone ought to help before he sighs himself away
line: Somebody ought to help that lad, before he sighs himself to death.

thought: her father's a lord; Romeo is Romeo
line: Her father's a lord, and Romeo's... well, Romeo.

thought: Draul Leptoc looks angry enough already
line: Draul Leptoc looks cross enough without Romeo hanging about.

thought: sees Romeo coming across the square
line: Oh, here comes Romeo. Look busy.

thought: Aris foresaw a demon; Aris says a lot
line: Aris says a demon's coming. Aris says a lot of things, mind.

thought: dark wizards at the circle, chanting
line: Those dark wizards at the circle are chanting. Never a good sign.

thought: Sir Prysin keeps the sword locked up
line: Sir Prysin's got the very sword that did for it. Locked up, naturally.

thought: three keys to one box; typical palace
line: Three keys to open one box. That's the palace for you.

thought: Captain Rovin only takes orders from the king
line: Captain Rovin takes orders from the king and nobody else, demon or no.

thought: will go round the stone circle the long way
line: I'll go round the stone circle the long way, thanks.

thought: nudges a friend: send that one for Aris's demon
line: Here, Aris keeps on about a demon. Send that one, they look idle.

thought: bathos: a demon, and the price of bread
line: A demon, of all things. And the price of bread what it is.

thought: Prysin's great-grandfather sealed it; runs in families
line: Sealed by Sir Prysin's great-grandfather, it was. Runs in families.

thought: would rather flee to Falador than face a demon
line: If that demon gets out, I'll be in Falador. And I don't like Falador.

thought: the circle is on the Lumbridge road; adventurers pass it daily
line: That circle's on the Lumbridge road. You lot walk past it daily.

thought: the demon's name sounds like a cough
line: Delrith, it's called. Sounds like a cough.

thought: nobody at the palace seems bothered
line: Nobody at the palace seems bothered. They're never bothered.

thought: a hundred and fifty years since Wally; a good run
line: A hundred and fifty years since the last demon. We had a good run.

thought: you give the fortune-teller a coin, she gives you a demon
line: Fortune-tellers. You give her a coin, she gives you a demon.

thought: the museum's Silverlight has a new card; that's this one
line: Saw the new card on Silverlight in the museum. That's you, isn't it?

thought: Wally is still talked about; this one will be too
line: They still talk about Wally. They'll talk about you, I expect.

thought: the circle is quiet now
line: The stone circle's quiet now. Thank you for that.

thought: points them out to a friend
line: Here, that's the one who did for the demon. No, don't point.

thought: saw off a demon and still does errands
line: Saw off a demon and still out doing errands. Fair play.

thought: will walk the Lumbridge road again, wizards or no
line: I'll walk the Lumbridge road again now. Wizards or no wizards.

thought: slept through the whole demon business
line: A demon in the circle, and I slept through the lot.

thought: recognises the one who took up Silverlight
line: You're the one who took up Silverlight, aren't you? Thought so.

thought: Wally's great-grandson Prysin; Wally would have shaken their hand
line: Sir Prysin's great-grandfather would've shaken your hand.

thought: the city sleeps easier
line: Varrock sleeps a bit easier, thanks to you. I know I do.

thought: the Herald should have had them on the front
line: The Herald ought to have had you on the front, demon and all.

thought: didn't look like a demon-slayer; shows what they know
line: Didn't look much like a demon-slayer, I thought. Shows what I know.

thought: would stand them a cup of tea
line: I'd stand you a cup of tea for that, I would.

thought: Captain Rovin won't say it, but the guard was glad
line: Captain Rovin won't say so, but I'd wager the guard was glad of you.

thought: a demon at their own circle, sorted by walking down
line: Our own stone circle, and you just walked down and sorted it.

thought: Gertrude has called herself hoarse
line: Gertrude's still out calling for Fluffs. Hoarse, she is, poor thing.

thought: a houseful of cats and she cries over one
line: Cats all over Gertrude's house, and it's Fluffs she cries for.

thought: Shilop selling information about a cat
line: Shilop's selling information now. About a cat. At his age.

thought: the boys play in the square while Gertrude frets
line: Wilough and Shilop in the square again, and their mother worried sick.

thought: four boys, all those cats, and now Fluffs gone
line: Four boys and all those cats, and now Fluffs gone. Poor woman.

thought: cats wander and come back hungry
line: Fluffs has wandered off, they say. Cats do, when they've a mind to.

thought: Gertrude asked if they'd seen a cat; they've seen hundreds
line: Gertrude stopped me in the road. Had I seen a cat? I've seen hundreds.

thought: with four boys in the house, the cat had reason to leave
line: If I were Fluffs I'd have run off too, with four boys in the house.

thought: someone should look before Gertrude has a turn
line: Somebody ought to find that cat before Gertrude has a turn.

thought: Gertrude wants anyone at all to find the cat, even an adventurer
line: Gertrude wants anyone at all to find Fluffs. Even an adventurer.

thought: so many cats and loses one
line: Never seen a woman with so many cats lose one. Careless, that.

thought: a lost cat is the most the Herald will get
line: Lost cat, west of the city. That's the Herald sorted for the week.

thought: the whole street calling for Fluffs, even the cats
line: She's got the whole street calling for Fluffs. Even the cats.

thought: the cat's name; as if it'd answer
line: Fluffs, she calls it. Fluffs! As if a cat would answer to that.

thought: folk by the Cooks' Guild looking under hedges
line: Out by the Cooks' Guild they're all looking under hedges for that cat.

thought: nobody would have looked in the Lumber Yard
line: The Lumber Yard, of all places! Nobody'd have looked there but you.

thought: Gertrude is happier since Fluffs came home
line: Gertrude's that much happier since you brought Fluffs home.

thought: went for one cat, came back with two
line: Two cats home for the price of one. That's good work.

thought: Gertrude sells kittens now; that's their doing
line: Gertrude's selling kittens now. I'd say that's your doing.

thought: points them out; would have looked too, of course
line: Here, that's who found Gertrude's Fluffs. Mind, I'd have looked too.

thought: most wouldn't bother about a cat
line: It's nice when somebody bothers about a cat. Most wouldn't.

thought: not every adventurer stoops to a lost cat
line: Not every adventurer would stoop to a lost cat. Fair play.

thought: Gertrude talks about them; she talks a lot anyway
line: Gertrude can't stop talking about you. Mind, she can't stop talking.

thought: speaker's own cat has gone off too; wonders if they do two
line: My cat's been off three days. Wonder if they'd do two.

thought: Fluffs suits motherhood
line: Fluffs looks well on it. Motherhood suits her.

thought: a busy woman with her hands full
line: That was a kind thing, for a busy woman with her hands full.

thought: four boys in that house and the stranger found the cat
line: Four boys and a houseful of cats, and you're the one who found Fluffs.

thought: the whole house purrs now
line: Gertrude's whole house is purring now, thanks to you.

thought: every lost cat in Varrock will follow them now
line: You'll have every lost cat in Varrock following you now.

thought: Fluffs looks like a scratcher
line: Did Fluffs scratch you? She looks the type.

thought: the city began round Arrav; the player did right by him
line: Varrock grew up round Arrav, they say. You did right by him.

thought: the Arrav from the museum, and they crossed swords with him
line: Arrav, him in the museum? And you crossed swords with him?

thought: the museum calls Arrav the best-known hero; they'll want this one
line: The museum calls Arrav our best-known hero. They'll want you next.

thought: Elias White is still at it, but this one got furthest
line: Elias White's still looking, I hear, but you got further than anyone.

thought: robbed a necromancer; speaker can't get a ladder back
line: Robbed a necromancer. I can't get my neighbour to return a ladder.

thought: points them out quietly
line: Here, that's the one who went into the necromancer's vault. Hush.

thought: wouldn't even say the necromancer's name
line: Zemouregal... I'd not even say the name. And they went in.

thought: Arrav kept as a servant; at least someone is trying
line: Poor Arrav, kept like a servant. At least someone's trying, eh?

thought: Varrock's own hero needed rescuing, and they went
line: Our own hero needed rescuing, and you went. Fair play.

thought: in and out of the vault; speaker would not have come out
line: Into the vault and out again. I'd not have come out, I know that.

thought: the heart was still beating; they kept their nerve
line: Still beating, the heart was, I heard. You kept your nerve, then.

thought: sober: Arrav deserved better
line: Arrav deserved better than that necromancer. Thank you for trying.

thought: they'll be in the museum one day too
line: You'll be in the museum yourself one day, next to Arrav.

thought: necromancers and vaults put their own hard day in proportion
line: Necromancers, vaults... and I thought my day was hard.

thought: stole from a necromancer and walks about in daylight
line: Not many would rob a necromancer and then stroll about in daylight.

thought: the delegation is due; the square is excited
line: The Varlamore lot are due at the palace. The square's in a fever.

thought: a treaty with King Roald
line: A treaty with Varlamore, they say. King Roald's signing it himself.

thought: bards at the Blue Moon went on about Varlamore
line: Bards in the Blue Moon went on about Varlamore half the night.

thought: they worship sun and moon both; greedy
line: They worship the sun over there, and the moon. Both! Greedy, that is.

thought: Alina's keen, Noah won't budge
line: Alina's packed already, I shouldn't wonder. Noah won't budge.

thought: a Sun Queen; imagine our king in a sun hat
line: A Sun Queen, they've got. Imagine our king in a sun hat.

thought: shut for centuries, now wanting trade
line: Shut up tight for hundreds of years, and now they want to trade.

thought: across the western sea; further than Falador
line: Across the western sea, Varlamore is. Further than Falador, anyway.

thought: the Herald says the delegation is coming; the Herald says a lot
line: The Herald says the delegation's coming. The Herald says a lot.

thought: waiting in the square to see foreigners, as if there were none here
line: Everyone's waiting in the square to see foreigners. As if we've none.

thought: a kingdom opening for trade will want Varrock's tea
line: Varlamore'll be wanting our tea next, I expect. Everyone does.

thought: sun and moon worshippers; the church will have views
line: Sun and moon worshippers due at the palace. The church'll have views.

thought: the Shining Kingdom; will believe it when it shines
line: I'll believe this Shining Kingdom when I see it shine.

thought: the guards on the square are half new faces
line: Guards all over the square for the delegation, and half of them new.

thought: Alina has talked of nothing else since the bards
line: Alina's talked of nothing but Varlamore since the bards came through.
